services.name: Past Exhibits
services.desc: We have more than 30,000 objects in our collection, and it continues to grow. That means to share more of the collection and the stories behind the objects, some of our exhibits will have to be retired periodically. But it does take months to create a major exhibit. As a result, we are exploring new ways (with the help of Univ. of Washington Researchers) to capture exhibits so that they continue to bring value even after they are gone. So, this section will continue to evolve as we come up with new approaches. services.name: Winter Cabin Market
services.desc: The Edmonds Winter Cabin Market is held in downtown Edmonds on 5th Avenue North at 118 5th Ave N, Edmonds, WA 98020. The Edmonds Winter Cabin Market, formerly known as the Winter Market, brings the spirit of the city’s popular outdoor markets into the quieter months of January through April. The market offers residents and visitors a welcome reason to get outside, reconnect with neighbors, and enjoy the community while waiting for spring. Local farmers, food producers, artisans, bakers, and makers line Fifth Avenue North between Main and Bell, offering seasonal foods, handcrafted goods, and other locally produced items. services.name: Bakery Audio Tour
services.desc: Our building limit currently at any one time is roughly 40, so if there are more scheduling shifts will be required. For larger classes, typically the class will be split between the upper and lower floors, and then will switch after a time. For smaller groups, the tour will flow through the entire Museum. If there is a focus on a particular topic, let us know and we will do our best to accommodate your interests. To schedule a tour, contact education@historicedmonds.org. Please provide enough advanced time for scheduling so we can ensure staff and volunteers will be available for your tour. services.name: Farm to Table
services.desc: Stop by the museum to take a bite of history at our latest exhibit on the local history of farming, cooking, and restaurants! It is a celebration of the rich history of farming, general stores, and restaurants in South Snohomish County at the Edmonds Historical Museum’s latest exhibit! The Edmonds Historical Museum is proud to partner with the Edmonds Food Bank to keep our community fed! Bring a non-perishable donation to the food bank to the exhibit opening for free entrance. The museum also thanks Shazad Raja from Caravan Kebab, Mai Tran from Rise and Shine Bakery, the Edmonds Bakery, and Shubert Ho’s Feed Me Hospitality and Restaurant Group for catering the opening.
